story: In 1992, astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail shocked the world by confirming the first planets ever detected outside our solar system. But they weren't orbiting a warm, sun-like star. Instead, they were found orbiting PSR B1257+12, a dead, rapidly spinning stellar remnant known as a millisecond pulsar. Located in the constellation Virgo, this extreme star rotates once every 6.2 milliseconds, blasting out regular beams of intense radio signals. By using the massive Arecibo radio telescope, Wolszczan measured tiny, periodic anomalies in these pulses, revealing three hidden worlds. Two of these alien planets are several times the mass of Earth, while the third is tiny, with a mass close to our Moon's. Bathed in constant, deadly radiation, these zombie worlds are completely hostile to life, likely forming from the debris of a violent cosmic collision.
angle: The very first confirmed planets discovered outside our solar system do not orbit a living star, but a rapidly spinning cosmic corpse that douses them in deadly radiation.
disputed: The exact distance to the pulsar is disputed; S1, S2, and S5 state it is 2,300 light-years away, while S6 states it is 1,500 light-years, S4 states ~500 parsecs (1,630 light-years), and S3 states 600 +/- 100 parsecs (1,950 light-years). The script should state that estimates range between 1,500 and 2,300 light-years.

The exact formation mechanism of the planets is uncertain; S1 mentions they likely formed from a white dwarf merger disk but notes supernova remnants or a quark-nova as other theories, while S5 describes them as 'zombie' planets formed from dust and gas of destroyed predecessor planets. The script should present these as theoretical possibilities rather than definitive fact.

A fourth planetary body in the system was reported in 1996 and 2005 (as detailed in S1 and S6), but was later retracted as the timing anomalies were explained by non-periodic dispersion changes. The script should leave out any claim of a fourth planet.
